title: From Expansion to Retraction: Long-tailed Machine Unlearning via Boundary Manipulation

problem.claim: Machine unlearning must remove information from specific data while retaining utility for remaining data.

gap.claim: Existing unlearning methods often assume balanced data and neglect long-tailed scenarios in which tail-class decision boundaries are distorted by insufficient representation.

contributions.claim: A Long-Tailed Machine Unlearning framework is proposed from a unified decision-boundary perspective.
The framework combines directional boundary repair for tail classes with boundary retraction that disperses augmented and original features throughout the feature space.
The framework provides a unified interpretation of the relationship between long-tailed learning and unlearning and enables flexible control through augmented-feature generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and neural network architectures demonstrate the framework's effectiveness in achieving complete unlearning of tail classes in long-tailed distributions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Machine unlearning removes information about specific data while preserving utility for remaining data.
Balanced-distribution assumptions leave existing methods ineffective when tail-class decision boundaries are distorted in long-tailed settings.
The paper introduces a long-tailed unlearning framework organized around unified decision-boundary manipulation.
Directional boundary repair enriches tail-class boundaries, followed by boundary retraction that disperses augmented and original features.
The authors report flexible repair and unlearning control and effective tail-class unlearning across multiple datasets and architectures.

source_observation.claim: The framework treats long-tailed learning and unlearning as related processes of decision-boundary manipulation.

interpretation.claim: For imbalanced-data unlearning, repairing underrepresented class boundaries may be a prerequisite for effective retraction.

application.claim: A staged repair-then-retraction design could guide unlearning systems operating on long-tailed distributions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design generalizes beyond the reported long-tailed settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, neural network architectures, baselines, metrics, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not specify how complete unlearning is measured or independently verified.
